text:
*Interview with Mademoiselle Lina Ruedi, régleuse, in the dining room. Second interview of the night.*

MATTHEY: Mademoiselle Ruedi, I am sorry to keep you up at this hour. Tell me first what your work is in this house.

MLLE RUEDI: I am the régleuse. I adjust the hairsprings and regulate the movements in the atelier. Monsieur Monnier taught me the work, and I think I am the best hand he had at the bench. I came down from a farm above Le Locle to do it.

MATTHEY: You worked beside him in the atelier.

MLLE RUEDI: Yes. I was at my bench beside his, until he sent me downstairs. He was exact in everything. A watch was either right or it was not, and he would tell you which.

MATTHEY: Let us come to the evening. What do you remember from dinner?

MLLE RUEDI: When the temple struck nine, the master made us all show our watches, as he did every year. He told each owner what was wrong with his. Mine was exact. I regulated it myself. Monsieur Félix's was twenty minutes behind. Monsieur Girard's was four minutes behind. The doctor's was two minutes ahead.

MATTHEY: And after dinner?

MLLE RUEDI: I worked beside the master in the atelier. When the temple struck ten, the regulator agreed with the bell exactly.

MATTHEY: You are sure of that?

MLLE RUEDI: I am sure of what I saw. It agreed exactly.

MATTHEY: What happened next?

MLLE RUEDI: He sent me downstairs when the regulator showed twenty past ten. The regulator was running then, and he was well.

MATTHEY: Did he say why he sent you down?

MLLE RUEDI: He did not say why. He did not often explain himself to me.

MATTHEY: Where did you go?

MLLE RUEDI: I went straight down to the kitchen, and I stayed there with Rosa from when I came down until after the temple struck eleven.

MATTHEY: Did you check your watch while you were in the kitchen?

MLLE RUEDI: I compared it with Rosa's clock. Her clock was exactly fifteen minutes fast.

MATTHEY: Did you hear anything from the upper floors?

MLLE RUEDI: From the kitchen we heard Madame's piano begin at twelve minutes to eleven by the kitchen clock, and stop at one minute past eleven by the kitchen clock. Madame plays Chopin. We could tell the pieces.

MATTHEY: You know the regulator in the atelier has stopped.

MLLE RUEDI: I did not see it stop. I can tell you only what it showed when I left.

MATTHEY: You have told me the master was working on a minute repeater. Can you tell me about it?

MLLE RUEDI: He worked on it for four years. A minute repeater speaks the time when you press the slide. The low notes are the hours. Each quarter is a doubled note. Then come the high notes, one for each minute past the quarter. He wanted the striking to be as exact as the going. It was the most exact thing he made.

MATTHEY: Do you know of anyone who wished him harm?

MLLE RUEDI: I do not know. I will not guess at what I did not see.

MATTHEY: Is there anything you wish to add?

MLLE RUEDI: Only that the regulator was running when he sent me down, and he was well. I would not say more than that.
